- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–3% relative to recent history.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect — apply a dampening factor (e.g., 0.95) to subsequent forecasts if prior 3-day average was > 75% of 30-day mean.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% if 30-day average is below 70 and recent 7-day average is falling.
- Forecast mean reversion is weak — if 30-day moving average is > 73, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 3 days; if < 70, increase by 0.5–1.0%.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to new data — if true outcome is > 1.5% above forecast at day 1, adjust next forecast down by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overcorrection.
- Avoid forecasting based on 30-day mean alone — incorporate 7-day rolling average to capture short-term momentum; if 7-day average > 30-day average, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0%.
